judged_text: Unbounded limit on the public members endpoint: limit = (params[:limit] || 50).to_i has no ceiling (old code capped automatic groups at 200), so limit=1000000 serializes the full membership of any visible group in one request — a mass user enumeration and DoS vector; also offset=-1 passes straight through to SQL (OFFSET -1) causing a 500

adjudication.rationale: In `GroupsController#members`, the diff introduces user-controlled pagination params applied to all groups without any bounding/sanitization: `limit = (params[:limit] || 50).to_i` and `offset = params[:offset].to_i`, then `group.users...limit(limit).offset(offset)`. There is no max cap on `limit`, so a request can ask for an extremely large page size, leading to very large DB work and response serialization (DoS/user enumeration risk) in a single request. `offset` is also not clamped to >= 0, so negative values are passed directly into the query via `.offset(offset)`, which can error depending on the DB/ORM behavior. (Note: the finding’s claim that the old code “capped automatic groups at 200” isn’t accurate because it still accepted `params[:limit]`, but the lack of a ceiling/offset validation in the new code is verifiable in the diff.)
